_comment: Universal KiCad / EE conventions shared by every module. NOT circuit-specific. Add new refdes letter codes here and every module picks them up.

power_symbol._comment: Schematic items that are not physical parts: power-port symbols, PWR_FLAG markers. Excluded from BOM and from basic-checks 'missing footprint' warnings.

missing_value_sentinels._comment: Strings that mean 'no value set' even though the field is non-empty. Case-insensitive.

refdes._comment: Per IEEE 315 / ANSI Y32.2. priority = sort order in BOM (lower = earlier). category = used by checks that key off part type.

grid._comment: KiCad default schematic grid. Symbols/wires off this grid silently fail to connect — checked by basic_checks.

defaults._comment: Footprints assigned to satellite parts (decoupling caps, pull-ups, freewheel diodes, current-limit R) that rules.py auto-inserts. Override here when switching to 0402 / 0805 house standard.

wire._comment: LAY_007 — power-net wires longer than this are flagged as defects (route them via power-port pairs instead).

chat._comment: Number of past chat turns kept in the Claude context window. Lower = cheaper but less continuity; higher = better recall but more tokens.

auto_no_connect._comment: Conservative auto-NC for floating pins. The connectivity_normalize pipeline inserts (no_connect) markers ONLY when a pin matches HIGH or SAFE confidence — never on power / clock / reset / analog / communication / differential / feedback. Patterns are CASE-INSENSITIVE; matched against the lib_symbol's pin name AFTER stripping leading ~. Each list is a substring/equality test — a pin name 'AVDD' matches 'AVDD' under unsafe_substrings. Add new patterns here as the user's MCU families surface them.

chat_snap._comment: Auto-snap thresholds for chat-applied ops. Claude often gives label/power-port coords that are 'near' a pin tip but not on it — causing KiCad to report `(no net)` for every label. The dispatcher silently snaps any label/power-port placed within snap_search_mm of a pin tip / wire endpoint to the exact coord, so port-name merging actually fires. Beyond max_snap_mm we refuse the op (genuinely dangling — Claude made a real mistake, surface it). junction_infer adds (junction ...) at every detected 3+ wire convergence after apply. power_port_dedup_mm collapses stacked duplicate power-ports at the same anchor.

chat_post_apply._comment: Post-apply normalization toggles. Each pass is idempotent — running twice produces the same result.

kicad_string_escapes._comment: KiCad serializes a few characters as {token} so they survive paths and identifiers. To compare or count net names correctly, un-escape them first. Extend as new tokens are observed in real schematics.
